To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microwave treatment of biomass Arthrospira sp. was more effective in the production of fermentable sugars than the conventional heating.
microwave heating can be used to increase the yield of ethanol in the process of alcoholic fermentation of cyanobacteria biomass.
the microwave heating is a very promising technique to improve the efficiency of the alcoholic fermentation of Arthrospira biomass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using cyanobacteria Arthropira platensis as a raw material for bioethanol production.
the possibility of using microwave heating to obtain fermentable sugars from biomass of A. platensis.
the possibility of using cyanobacteria biomass as an alternative substrate for bioethanol production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microwave heating of the biomass of Arthrospira sp. is an effective method of polysaccharidic material degradation and the subsequent alcohol fermentation process.
the microwave-heated substrate is a better source of fermentable sugars and a more effective source of alcohol than the conventional substrate.
the microwave-heated substrate was the most advantageous, and the obtained results were the best.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microwave heating is the most effective method of thermochemical treatment of cyanobacteria biomass, and it can be used as a pretreatment method for bioethanol production from cyanobacteria.

the microwave heating of the biomass of cyanobacterium Arthrospira sp. in a microwave oven with a power of 100 W at the temperature of 100 °C for 30 min is a good method of obtaining a fermentable substrate for the production of bioethanol.
the use of microwaves as a source of energy for the thermochemical hydrolyzation of cyanobacteria biomass can be considered as a promising method of bioethanol production.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the application of microwave heating in the process of thermodegradation of polysaccharidic substances in cyanobacterial biomass can be a useful method for obtaining fermentable sugars, which can be used for the production of bioethanol.
the microwave method of thermochemical hydrothermal treatment of biomass of cyanobacterial Arthrospira plantensis can be recommended as the method of choice for biofuel production.
the use of microwaves in the process of thermolysis is more beneficial than the use of conventional methods.
